The '''2026 City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council election''' took place on Thursday 7 May 2026, alongside [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections in the United Kingdom]]. All 90 members of the [[City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council]] in [[West Yorkshire]] were elected following boundary changes. The election in Idle and Thackley ward will take place in June 2026 following the death of a candidate.<ref name=Idle />

==Background==
Bradford was created in 1974 as a [[metropolitan borough]]. The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] formed a majority administration from its creation until [[1978 City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council election|1978]], when the council fell into [[no overall control]].<ref>{{cite web |title=BBC News - Election 2011 - England council elections - Bradford |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/special/election2011/council/html/cx.stm |website=BBC News |access-date=18 January 2026}}</ref> [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] won their first majority in [[1980 City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council election|1980]], and have been the only party to form majority administrations since. Aside from a brief period between [[2004 City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council election|2004]] and [[2006 City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council election|2006]], Labour have been the largest party on the council for the entirety of the 21st century and have continuously held a majority of seats since [[2014 City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council election|2014]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pidd |first1=Helen |title=Labour gains control of Bradford as Respect fails |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/the-northerner/2014/may/23/labour-gains-control-of-bradford-george-galloway-respect-fails |access-date=18 January 2026 |work=The Guardian |date=23 May 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=https://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Bradford-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=18 January 2026}}</ref>

[[2024 City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council election|2024]] saw Labour fall to its lowest number of councillors in eight years following large gains by [[Independent politician|independents]], which some attributed to Labour's stance on the [[Gaza war]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Labour retains Bradford City Council amid surge from independents |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cnd6e26k2k8o |access-date=18 January 2026 |work=BBC News |date=3 May 2024}}</ref> Labour won 10 seats (down 4), independents won 9 seats (up 4), the Conservatives won 4 seats (down 2), the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] won 4 seats (up 2) and the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] won 3 seats (steady). Following the election, the Conservatives formed a group with independent councillor Luke Majkowski.

This election took place on a new set of ward boundaries, meaning all 90 seats were up for election.<ref>[https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/461/made The Bradford (Electoral Changes) Order 2025]</ref>
